children.name: Sarcobatus baileyi Coville
children.description: A North American greasewood, one of two species of Sarcobatus (sole genus of family Sarcobataceae, order Caryophyllales; long placed in Chenopodiaceae). Native to California and Nevada in arid, often saline or alkaline Great Basin habitats, it is a spiny, deciduous shrub with succulent linear leaves, sometimes treated as a variety of the more widespread S. vermiculatus.

children.name: Sarcobatus vermiculatus  Torr.
children.description:
A common species on alkaline habitats (Hils et al. 1993), Sarcobatus vermiculatus was found in greatest abundance along the banks of a seasonally wet stream crossing due northeast of MDRS (Fig. 46). Previously placed within the Chenopodiaceae, Sarcobatus is now recognized as the sole genus within the Sarcobataceae (Behnke 1997; APG III 2009). This species was previously recorded for the nearby San Rafael Swell (Harris 1983).
